text.p: --BIRTHDAYS--
English social reformer Sir GEORGE WILLIAMS, who founded the YMCA, was born in 1821.
HENRY JOHN HEINZ, U.S. food-products manufacturer who formed H.J. Heinz Co, was born in 1844.
The German industrial chemist who invented the process of extracting oil from coal, FRIEDRICH BERGIUS, was born in 1884.

Former American first lady ELEANOR ROOSEVELT was born in New York City in 1884. She was married to FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT. ELEANOR was a social worker, lecturer and newspaper columnist. Her column "My Day" was syndicated widely throughout the country. She was a delegate to the United Nations' general assembly and chair of the UN commission on human rights. She helped draw up the Declaration of Human Rights at the UN in 1945.
American jazz drummer ART BLAKEY was born in 1919.

US singer, pianist and songwriter DARYL HALL (DARYL HOHL) was born in 1948. He was successful from 1976 with JOHN OATES in their duo of 'HALL and OATES'. Hits included "Rich Girl" (1977),"I Can't Go For That" (1981), "Maneater" (1982) and "Say It Isn't So" (1983) and "Out of Touch" (1984).
American saxophonist and flautist ANDREW WOOLFOLK was born in 1950. He played as a session musician and with 'Earth, Wind and Fire'.
--EVENTS--
1871 : The Great Fire of Chicago was finally extinguished
after three days.
1899 : The South African Boer War began between the
British Empire and Boers of the Transvaal and Orange Free State.
1919 : The first in-flight meals were served on board a
flight from London to Paris. Passengers had to pay three shillings each for the meal.
1931 : One of Australia's greatest generals Sir JOHN
MONASH was buried in high state. More than five thousand old soldiers marched by the Parliament in a last gesture of respect for their victorious leader in France.
1939 : Albert Einstein and other U.S scientists informed
President Roosevelt of the possibilities of developing an atomic bomb.
1947 : The first Indian cricket team to tour Australia
arrived in Perth.
1961 : The piano-playing Marx brother CHICO died.
1968 : Apollo 7 was launched with three astronauts on
board.
1976 : The third wife and widow of MAO TSE-TUNG, QIANG
QING, was arrested with three associates. The "Gang of Four" had attempted to seize power on MAO's death.
1980 : Soviet cosmonauts returned to earth after a record
185 days in space in Salyut 6.
1982 : The "Mary Rose", once HENRY VIII's flagship, was
raised from the Solent, off southern England.
1986 : Mother THERESA walked away from a plane crash in
Tanzania which killed six people.
1987 : A huge sonar exploration of Loch Ness failed to

find the Monster. The Scottish monster, affectionately known as Nessie, was allegedly first sighted by St COLUMBA in 565. Since then there have been hundreds of reported sightings and some photographic evidence. The search of the loch by 24 boats fitted with sonic detectors was controversial with some reports claiming they'd found a large moving object at a depth of around 58 metres.
1994 : The inquiry into the Cannonball Run accident in
which four people died in May, found that the Ferrari involved in the crash was travelling well above the designated speed for the event.
